question: Do a one-individual finite-population reproductive advantage and the population-wide response of viable-seed output have the same local sign, and when do F/P/S routes explain disagreement?
source: unmodified Model3 reproduce_kb and postzygotic baseline ledger
founder_state: Monomorphic synthetic clones with two identical copies at each of three loci; no evolving genetic trajectory.
numeric_stability_rule: stable sign and max absolute difference <= 0.02 + 0.05 * max(abs(h1),abs(h2)); otherwise inconclusive
individual_beta: one individual's log(.5*F_i + .5*P_i + S_i) difference under +/- trait shift while all other N-1 clones remain resident; at K8 one individual is 12.5% and this is NOT the infinite-population rare-mutant beta
group_gamma_seed: log(total viable self+outcross seeds) derivative when ALL N genotypes/expressed traits shifted by +/- equally
component_decomposition: symmetric log-mean denominator gives exact finite-difference additive beta_F+beta_P+beta_S; P is paternal outcross success of focal mutant, not automatically zero sum when group outcross total changes
outcomes: all raw numeric slopes including inconclusive cells
component fractions as descriptive values not causal mediation
scope_exclusions: NOT true rare mutant at finite K
implementation_gate: CI must run focused unit tests, exact source and input assertions, archive full machine JSON, verify source SHA and output before numeric interpretation
pending_next_stage: Using same defined phenotypes and new independent visitor histories, separately preregister Gamma_persist and evolution-enabled versus trait-clamped contrasts; do not reuse this engineering grid as confirmatory data
